Mâm Mâm will beam you out of this world (of taste).
Apr 2026 • Friends
We dined at Mâm Mâm yesterday evening at the invitation of our representative at TPBank. The modern interior is impressive—spacious with high ceilings and a clever, upside-down “mâm” (traditional Vietnamese serving tray) hovering above the dining area like a UFO.
Our party of three enjoyed a very pleasant evening. The modern Vietnamese cuisine was delicious and the portions were generous. The Tilapia sashimi and the dry-aged duck with shrimp crackers were standout starters that shifted our taste buds into high gear. For our main, the roasted chicken with bamboo-tube rice was beautifully presented; it was a refined take that stayed true to traditional flavors.
A special mention to Ms. Trang, who attended our table. She was truly outstanding—knowledgeable, confident, and added a creative touch to our dining experience. Highly recommended!

Insider tip:
Order extra Vietnamese shrimp crackers, they are addictive.

Mam Mam Vietnamese Eatery & Lounge - this place hits different
Jan 2026 • Family
Mam Mam is housed in the ground floor of Nexus, a rather new office building behind the waterfront Le Meridian Saigon Hotel, making it easily accessible yet not too close to the crowded, noisy part of District 1.

Many Viet restaurants these days are doing more of the same - elevating their dishes by using more expensive ingredients or have fancier plating.

We like the food here because it returns to origins i.e. it's cool to know how each dish are actually specialties from different parts of Vietnam AND using ingredients sourced from that specific region. From Dak Nong chicken and Phu Quoc fresh squid, to even knowing the seasonings of Tay Bac Oil (meaning from Northwestern Vietnam) or Hue shrimp paste, as well as matching sides like Bamboo Tube Rice popular among ethnic minorities from that region. It's like you learn something new as each dish tells a unique story. Palmyra cake from An Giang was fun and chewy.

We like the space because it's entirely open concept - wide open & beamless space, open kitchen, standalone bar, high ceiling framed by an impressively detailed painted mural of District 1's skyline, with a giant overhanging tray as its focal point. The gentle lighting makes it easier for relaxing and chilling over a drink (which reminded me their "Sour Tea" coupled with compressed tamarind was delicious!).

Prices are pretty easy on the wallet too.
Call to make reservations, as they seem to be booked for private events sometimes.
